      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives</p><p>African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.</p><p><a href="https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/see-my-world-film-festival-tickets-2000609164867">See My World</a>, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/08/african-philosophies-see-my-world-film-festival-manchester">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts">voters turning away from the party</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:20:22 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>The most hacked country in Europe? Why is France the target of so many cyberattacks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261111-the-most-hacked-country-in-europe-why-is-france-the-target-of-so-many-cyberattacks</link><description>
The “unprecedented” hacks of French supermarket refrigerators were the latest in a series of major cyberattacks that have made the country the most hacked in Europe, according to some analysts. Cyberattacks are on the rise globally, but why is France such a ready target?  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bfa44840-dde7-11f1-9104-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100233Z-802993939-RC282OALI9O2-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bfa44840-dde7-11f1-9104-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100233Z-802993939-RC282OALI9O2-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e06572f8-dde6-11f1-969d-af2cc4d94f00</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:09:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bfa44840-dde7-11f1-9104-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100233Z-802993939-RC282OALI9O2-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg">© Lucien Libert, Reuters</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days afer shootings</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tens-of-thousands-attend-polish-nationalist-march-days-afer-shootings</link><description>
Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw Wednesday for an annual Independence Day March, just days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow that shook the country. The event is held each November 11 to commemorate the ending in 1918 of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria. While generally peaceful, some rallies in the pasthave been marred by clashes with police or counter-demonstrators. Philip Turle gives us his take.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/632a3764-ddf1-11f1-a19a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261111-171020-171438-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/632a3764-ddf1-11f1-a19a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261111-171020-171438-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">68843412-ddf1-11f1-9583-93ccc3b6b1f8</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:08:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Tehran will strike US bases in Europe if used to attack Iran, security chief says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261111-tehran-will-strike-us-bases-in-europe-if-used-to-attack-iran-security-chief-says</link><description>
Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Wednesday that Tehran would attack US bases located in Europe if they were used to carry out bombing raids against the Islamic republic. The heavy defeat of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections earlier this month seems to have pushed Washington to pull back its threats to carry out fresh strikes against Iran.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f8c593d6-ddec-11f1-8f0b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26234800648076.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f8c593d6-ddec-11f1-8f0b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26234800648076.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">24968058-ddeb-11f1-8557-1dfefa073200</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:45:46 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f8c593d6-ddec-11f1-8f0b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26234800648076.jpg">© Vahid Salemi, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Haiti: 'We need to know the truth, but so far, it’s totally dark'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/bukele-says-salvadoran-troops-destroyed-gang-hq-in-haiti</link><description>
Jean-Marie Théodat, Director of the Department of Geography at University Paris, is our guest.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2f6655d8-dded-11f1-926e-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261111-151842-152903-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2f6655d8-dded-11f1-926e-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261111-151842-152903-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33f1f422-dded-11f1-8600-530574a1d80e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:38:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Violent incidents in schools as French students vow to maintain protest pressure</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/violent-incidents-in-schools-as-french-students-vow-to-maintain-protest-pressure</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron on Tuesday condemned violence against teachers andgovernment officials during nationwide street protests after an official was hit by a gasoline-filled bottle outside ​a high school ‌near Paris.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/09a5a02c-ddf4-11f1-b670-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-2c78d2b9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/09a5a02c-ddf4-11f1-b670-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-2c78d2b9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">610b121a-ddeb-11f1-a193-5f9177961f63</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:35:05 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description>Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday as two days of US mediated talks concluded, but they announced no major breakthrough on ending the conflict that began after Moscow’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.

      <description>China’s infantry units are adapting to the growing threat from drones, with some brigades introducing compulsory counter-drone training, new equipment and fresh tactics to help soldiers evade aerial surveillance and attacks.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore ]]> The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet.

Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth.

Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth.

"Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement.

Stripping the romance from the Earth's turbulent past

Comet impacts on Earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets.

For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely.

Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves.

In particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS.

The problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second).

Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry.

"It would really have to be a one-in-a-million occurrence, because not only would you need an impact at just the right speed and just the right angle, you would also need everything to happen after that point, in terms of the concentration and the speed at which the chemical origins of life got going," said Anslow. "We can’t rule out for certain that it happened that way, but it seems to be a really rare occurrence – at best, a one-off fluke."

Maybe life on Earth is a fluke

It is not yet known if the origin of life on Earth was a fluke, or whether life is plentiful in the universe, so a fluke occurrence could still have been a trigger for life on our planet.

However, researchers are coming around to alternatives, either that all the pre-biotic chemistry that resulted in life took place on Earth without requiring material from space, or asteroids instead brought those important molecules to Earth.

Scientists have found asteroids to be rich in those molecules – for example, the sample of material brought back by the OSIRIS-REx mission from the near-Earth asteroid Bennu contained all the building blocks of RNA.

However, other planets could have plausibly benefitted from comet impacts. The simulations showed that complex organic molecules in comets would stand a slightly better chance of surviving impacts on Mars, because of the Red Planet’s thinner atmosphere and lower gravity.

"This is not to say it definitely happened on Mars, of course, but it suggests it would be unlikely if it happened on Earth and didn’t happen on Mars," said Anslow. "Or the other, perhaps more likely, alternative is that it didn’t happen on either planet."

More intriguing are the possibilities on exoplanets, specifically the peas-in-a-pod multi-planet systems around red dwarf stars such as TRAPPIST-1, where all the planets are bunched up close.

In 2023 Anslow wrote a research paper describing how comets could gravitationally bounce from one planet to the next, losing velocity in the process so that when they crash into one of the planets, they impact is not so severe and complex organic molecules might have a chance to survive.

The team's research was published on 28 October in Scientific Reports.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million ]]> The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground.

Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027.

"Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We saw a pent-up launch market on the horizon, and rather than provide early discounted launches, we set out to deliver a rocket into an environment with extreme demand at full price or higher."

Rocket Lab is best known for Electron, a workhorse small-satellite launcher that debuted in 2017 and now has 90 orbital missions under its belt. The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO).

Neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO.

Rocket Lab announced Neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control).

Such setbacks have not dampened demand for Neutron's services, however. During Monday's call, Beck revealed that Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches during the third quarter of 2026, which ran from July 1 through Sept. 30.

The contracts for those eight flights are worth "a total of roughly 515 million, including multiple missions on a new escalated base price of $70 million," Beck said. Neutron's first 16 launches are now sold out, he added, and bookings from here on will be for flights in the 2030s.

"The demand is a function of both a tightening global launch supply and our customers' confidence that Rocket Lab is the right partner to break the world's launch bottleneck," Beck said.

That bottleneck is coming in 2028 or so, when SpaceX plans to retire its Falcon 9 rocket. For some perspective, and comparison with Neutron: SpaceX currently charges $74 million for each Falcon 9 launch. The rocket has a reusable first stage and can carry about 25 tons (22.7 metric tons) to LEO.

The medium lifter has been the world's most prolific rocket for the past few years. In 2025, for example, it flew 165 times — roughly the same number of orbital missions as all other launchers in the world combined. And all 165 of those flights were successful.

But SpaceX is phasing out the Falcon 9 — and its heavy-lift cousin, the Falcon Heavy — nonetheless, shifting all launch work over to its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which can haul more than 100 tons to LEO.

There's a real worry among folks in the space community that this massive payload capacity won't be available to them for a while. SpaceX has made it pretty clear that early Starship operations will be geared toward internal priorities — specifically, the buildout of SpaceX's Starlink V3 broadband network and its Starmind AI data-center constellation.

These will be very big jobs, even for the most powerful rocket ever built. For example, the Starlink V3 megaconstellation will consist of about 100,000 satellites, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk. Starship can carry about 60 of these spacecraft to LEO per launch, so just building out the constellation will require about 1,700 liftoffs.

The numbers for Starmind will be even more mind-boggling, for SpaceX wants that constellation to eventually harbor a million satellites.

The coming launch bottleneck should increase demand for Electron as well as Neutron, Beck said during Monday's call. After all, many small-satellite operators have launched with SpaceX over the years, booking spots on Falcon 9 "rideshare" flights. And those opportunities are now drying up.

"The next logical alternative is of course an Electron, so we see tremendous traction there," Beck said.

]]> <![CDATA[ Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026 ]]> The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange.

But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed.

What is it?

The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus.

M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity.

Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old!

Why is it amazing

Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell.

Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history.

Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus.

Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old!

Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell.

Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history.

The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum.

UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement.

"The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement.

UVEX will paint a picture of cosmic life, death and afterlife

UVEX will benefit from a major leap forward in UV sensitivity thanks to its Caltech-built sensors, which are based on complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) imaging technology. This will help the spacecraft tap into what Harrison described as "the untapped opportunity in the UV."

UVEX will be uniquely poised to spot millions of nearby, small, and faint galaxies that are teeming with infant stars that emit bright UV light.

"In optical light, it's very hard to distinguish these nearby galaxies from faraway ones that look similar," Harrison said. "UV light will make them easier to find."

UVEX won't just be investigating the infancy of stars, however. It will also examine the deaths of ancient stars in the form of supernovas.

Supernovas occur when a massive star runs out of fuel for nuclear fusion and can no longer support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the core of the star collapses, its outer layers are blasted outward in cosmic explosions we call supernovas.

This is a process that scientists are keen to understand, as these explosions fling the heavy elements forged during the stars' lifetimes into surrounding galaxies. This material becomes the building blocks of the next generation of stars, planets, and possibly even life.

UVEX will also investigate what happens to the end products of some supernovas, neutron stars, when they meet and merge.

Neutron stars contain between one and two times the mass of the sun crammed into a width of around 12 miles (20 kilometers). That means they are composed of matter so dense that, if a teaspoon of it were brought to Earth, it would weigh over 1 billion tons. That's equivalent to stacking around 9 million adult blue whales on a spoon.

So, when neutron stars in binary systems spiral together and merge, they create an environment so violent that it's the only place in the universe where scientists are sure that elements heavier than lead, like gold, silver, and platinum, are able to be forged.

Currently, neutron star mergers are detected via ripples in spacetime called gravitational waves. Scientists can then follow up on the aftermath of the mergers by observing them in electromagnetic light, from high-energy gamma rays to low-energy radio waves. Thus, UVEX will add another aspect to the investigation of neutron star collisions and our understanding of where heavy elements originate.

The new space telescope's maneuverability will allow it to observe these explosive events very shortly after they happen, giving it an advantage over other instruments, including NASA's long-serving Hubble Space Telescope.

"With UVEX, we will now be able to follow up on gravitational-wave events in ultraviolet light," UVEX team member and Caltech scientist Mansi Kasliwal said in the same statement. "I can count on two hands how many spectra we have of transient events in their infancy phase with the Hubble Space Telescope. Hubble is, of course, amazing and does have some ultraviolet capabilities, but it cannot rapidly pivot to observe real-time events."

UVEX will also be revolutionary in the study of blue stars that have had their outer layers of hydrogen stripped away by companion stars. These stars offer researchers a unique opportunity to study the interior of stars, which is usually obscured by their outer layers.

"We will be able to see what's inside the stars," Kareem El-Badry, an associate professor of astronomy at Caltech and a member of the UVEX team, said in the same statement. "We only know of a small number of stripped stars of this type now. UVEX will find hundreds."

All of the above elements discussed are the expected discoveries and investigations that UVEX will be involved with. Perhaps even more exciting, however, are the unexpected elements of the universe it will uncover.

"Every time you look at the skies in a new wavelength, you learn something new and unexpected," El-Badry said.

]]> <![CDATA[ Why I recommend the Seestar S30 Plus smart telescope for beginners — full review ]]> I’ve used several smart telescopes over the last few years, but I'd recommend the ZWO Seestar S30 Plus to almost anyone wanting to get started in astrophotography. At $499/€499, it’s a complete imaging system that can photograph galaxies, nebulae and star clusters automatically, even from a light-polluted city. Better still, it’s so small that it can live on a bookshelf.

I recently captured images of the Dumbbell Nebula (M27), the North America Nebula (NGC 7000), the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) and the Pleiades (M45) with the S30 Plus. All were remarkably easy to capture, and none of the images accompanying this review required external processing. It’s basically point-and-shoot astrophotography — if you live under light-polluted skies, that’s a game-changer.

I also think the S30 Plus makes an ideal companion to a conventional optical telescope. I can set it to photograph a nebula I have no hope of seeing under light pollution while I try to find brighter objects through the eyepiece of another telescope. It will then get on with collecting photons while I enjoy observing.

For anyone who already owns a telescope but doesn’t want the expense and complexity of conventional astrophotography, that’s a compelling proposition.

I photographed nebulas despite light pollution

One problem with buying a cheap optical telescope is that deep-sky objects rarely resemble the colorful photographs you see online. The moon, planets and bright star clusters can look wonderful through an eyepiece, but faint galaxies and nebulas are much harder to appreciate, particularly from a town or city.

Like all smart telescopes, the S30 Plus gets around that problem by photographing objects rather than showing them directly. Its camera takes repeated exposures, which the telescope automatically stacks to reduce noise and gradually reveal faint detail. The longer you leave it working, the better the resulting image tends to become.

Being able to photograph colorful nebulas without traveling to a remote observing site is one of the biggest attractions of the S30 Plus. For beginners living in cities, it could transform their experience of astronomy.

It’s the perfect companion to my optical telescope

I’ve always preferred spending my nights looking at the sky rather than fiddling with equipment, which is one reason I enjoy smart telescopes. Traditional astrophotography can involve a camera, tracking mount, adapters, cables, alignment, a laptop and considerable patience before the first useful exposure begins. The S30 Plus removes almost all of that.

I can put it outside, connect the Seestar app and choose a target from its built-in sky atlas. The telescope then moves to the correct position, identifies the star field, centers the object, focuses and begins imaging. Within minutes, a photograph starts appearing on my smartphone. That leaves me free to use an optical telescope alongside it — or stay inside and do something else.

The longer I leave it alone, the better the images get

Using the S30 Plus’s built-in UV/IR cut filter — which blocks ultraviolet and infrared light — I captured the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), a popular deep-sky object. As the hours went by, the dust lanes on its outskirts appeared in ever more detail. That’s how smart telescopes work — they collect and combine dozens or hundreds of short exposures, gradually revealing fainter structure while reducing noise.

So impressive is the image after only about five or six exposures that it’s tempting to stop after a few minutes — but patience makes an enormous difference. Fortunately, you don’t have to stand beside the S30 Plus. You can leave it collecting light — even overnight, thanks to its scheduling option (though it’s not waterproof, so check the weather forecast!).

Using the dual-band anti-light pollution filter, the Pleiades open cluster (M45) provided another interesting test. The S30 Plus has a mosaic mode that photographs overlapping sections of sky to create a larger image than its main camera can capture in a single frame. It’s ideal for expansive targets such as the Pleiades and Andromeda, although gathering enough exposures takes time. The app shows how much of the mosaic has been completed, and if needs be, you can continue collecting data on subsequent nights.

I also photographed the Double Cluster in Perseus (NGC 869 and NGC 884) and the Great Globular Cluster in Hercules (M13), both relatively swift targets, but as anyone who’s used a smart telescope knows, it’s the faint nebulas that are the real prize. For those, dark skies mean better data — and that’s exactly why a smart telescope needs to be portable.

It’s small enough to fit in my camera bag

The S30 Plus weighs just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg) and measures 8.25 x 5.5 x 3.15 inches (210 x 140 x 80 mm) when switched off. That’s small enough to fit into a camera bag in place of another lens or camera body, which is a major advantage because I travel to remote locations quite frequently. That fact that it sits on such a tiny tripod is also a boon.

I’ve recently used the much larger Seestar S50 Pro, which weighs 6.17 lbs (2.8 kg). It’s a more capable imaging instrument with a 50mm aperture and a larger 8.3-megapixel sensor, but its heavier, bulkier chassis is harder to get into carry-on luggage. The S30 Plus and the higher-spec S30 Pro also differ from the S50 Pro in that they come with a padded carry case. This has a useful carrying handle, although there’s no shoulder strap or dedicated storage for the tripod and magnetic solar filter.

It’s also worth taking along a portable battery and USB-C cable to recharge its built-in 6,000mAh battery during long sessions, though it lasts about six hours, which will suit most observing sessions.

It’s much more advanced than the original S30

The original, now-discontinued S30 was already impressive, but the S30 Plus is a substantial upgrade. It has improved four-element apochromatic optics with ED glass and two 3.7-megapixel cameras, each producing 1,440x2,560-pixel images. That’s almost 80% more pixels than the original S30’s main camera.

The main camera’s field of view has increased slightly to about three degrees, while the wide-angle camera now covers 43.5 degrees of sky. The latter can be used for star trails, though I suspect it’s something most people will experiment with occasionally.

There’s also an EQ mode. This will align the telescope with Earth’s rotation to allow longer exposures and sharper edges, which I found worked really well. It requires an appropriately angled mount or wedge (such as the Seestar TH10 Fluid Tripod Head) and a small tripod.

I tested it at 51 degrees north, which randomly appears to be the cut-off point for ease of use because of the tilt it puts on the telescope. It’s when a tripod begins to topple with the weight, meaning you need a tripod whose legs can be set at a low angle (Seestar’s TC20 tripod would be ideal, and is very compact).

The app makes it all very easy to set up, and advanced imaging possibilities like this are welcome. So, too, is the option of outputting images as lossless FITS files for anyone wanting to process their images using specialist software.

That’s what makes the Seestar S30 Plus such a good beginner’s telescope. It’s easy to use immediately, but there’s plenty of scope to develop more sophisticated astrophotography skills without buying another instrument.

I photographed the moon and sun during the day

The S30 Plus isn’t limited to deep-sky photography. I photographed a near-full moon against a blue daytime sky, something I particularly enjoy doing with smart telescopes because they’re so quick to set up.

It also comes with a magnetic white-light solar filter, allowing safe photographs of the sun when the filter is securely fitted. This must always be installed before pointing the telescope towards the sun. I did have to manually guide the S30 Plus to the sun and moon on a few occasions, but it’s easy enough to do, and I actually like the option to manually take control — few other smart telescopes allow it. Once you’ve found the sun or moon, the scope centers it and keeps it in view (unless you’re on a moving ship, by the way, where tracking generally fails — something for eclipse chasers to think about).

Planetary photography is less impressive. The 30mm aperture and short focal length aren’t ideal for detailed views of Jupiter or Saturn, so for anyone primarily interested in observing and imaging planets, I’d recommend a conventional optical telescope instead.

I could spend years exploring the sky with this telescope

The S30 Plus occupies an interesting position in ZWO’s increasingly crowded Seestar range. With dual 8.3MP cameras and wider fields of view, the S30 Pro is a worthy upgrade from the original S30. Meanwhile, the $999 S50 Pro has a larger 50mm aperture that collects almost three times as much light, although it’s also significantly bulkier and more expensive.

Alternatives exist outside ZWO’s range. DwarfLab’s Dwarf Mini is exceptionally portable, but its lower resolution and more limited capabilities make it less versatile. At the other extreme, Unistellar’s Odyssey has an 85mm aperture, an electronic eyepiece and opportunities to contribute to citizen science projects, but it sits in a different price bracket.

The S30 Plus will hit the sweet spot for many. It offers almost everything a beginner needs to explore deep-sky astrophotography, with built-in filters, mosaic mode and EQ tracking giving plenty of advanced features to grow into. Crucially, it’s small enough to travel with easily. Yes, you can spend more and get slightly better image data, but most beginners don’t need to.

The Seestar S30 Plus is one of the most affordable smart telescopes available, but it’s also one of the best-value offerings in its class.

]]> <![CDATA[ What time will SpaceX launch Starship Flight 15, its 1st double landing test, on Nov. 13? (Full mission timeline) ]]>

SpaceX is just days away from what might be its most ambitious test flight yet of the company's massive Starship megarocket, the largest launch vehicle ever built.

On Friday (Nov. 13), SpaceX will launch its next Starship test flight on a mission that, if successful, will return both its Super Heavy first-stage booster and Ship upper stage to Earth for back-to-back landings at their launch pad. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. And if you want to watch it live, you'll need to know what time and where to tune in.

In our guide below, we'll explain exactly when and how to watch SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 mission. It is the 15th test flight of the giant stainless-steel reusable rocket, which SpaceX wants to use for everything from Starlink internet satellite launches to landing NASA Artemis astronauts on the moon in 2028, and even for a crewed flight to Mars. But first, SpaceX has to successfully recover and refly both stages, something it's never done before — and that's where Flight 15 comes in. It's the first time the company will try to land an entire Starship rocket. Here's when to tune in.

What time is SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launch (and landing)?

The Starship Flight 15 test mission is currently scheduled to launch no earlier than Friday, Nov. 13, at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT), from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. But there is a chance of a later liftoff time.

SpaceX has said it has a 75-minute window in which to launch Starship Flight 15 to add some flexibility into its preflight countdown. ]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos) ]]> SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket.

The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13).

During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history.

Booster 22 therefore "was used for final catch testing upon arrival [at the pad], including a suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX said in an X post today (Nov. 10).

That post shared four photos of the giant booster, which is powered by 33 of SpaceX's next-gen Raptor engines. The first shot showed Super Heavy in one of Starbase's "Mega Bay" assembly buildings before rollout, while the other three depicted it grasped by the tower's arms, held high in the South Texas sky.

SpaceX has used the chopstick arms during Starship flights before; it has successfully caught Super Heavy on three separate occasions. But the company has never attempted a catch of Ship, which flies higher and farther than the booster and is therefore a more challenging target. And SpaceX only reached orbit with Starship for the first time on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28.

So Flight 15 will break new ground. And, if all goes to plan, it will give us a look at the future: SpaceX plans to catch Super Heavy and Ship on all operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will allow the company to boost the megarocket's launch cadence.

And SpaceX wants to fly Starship incredibly often, so that it can build out its Starlink V3 broadband constellation and even bigger Starmind AI data-center network. Indeed, Elon Musk has said the company is eyeing 10,000 Starship flights per year by 2030.

If all goes to plan, Flight 15 will launch from Starbase on Friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time).

Super Heavy will return to Starbase for its catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. Ship will follow suit much later — about 22 hours later, in fact, after it has deployed 26 Starlink V3 spacecraft into LEO and completed 14 circuits of our planet.

You can watch all the action live here at Space.com and get updates about the mission here.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field ]]>

On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field.

GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel.

At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth. Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage.

It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity, mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents.

Why it mattered

The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname.

"GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description.

There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude.

GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space, leading to a fiery plunge to Earth.

The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface.

]]> <![CDATA[ A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why ]]> Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet.

The exoplanet, designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a "hot Jupiter."

However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished.

This team used TESS data to determine that TOI-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. This is causing the orbits of both worlds in the TOI-2535 system to "wobble." TOI-2535 b disappeared when that wobble tilted it out of alignment with its star.

"We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that's not true. If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other's orbits. We know of a few systems that are like this," team member Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, said in a statement. "This is the most extreme example we've seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching."

TOI-2535 b isn't expected to transit its parent star for at least 30 years, but the hidden neighbor tugging on it may cross the face of the star sooner than that.

In the meantime, scientists will attempt to decode what this extreme wobbling exoplanet system says about how it formed.

Hot Jupiters should be cool customers

There is currently a lot of speculation about how hot Jupiter planets like TOI-2535 b form. That is because current routes of planet formation suggest planets like this would need to form around a great deal of ice. Obviously, ice isn't likely to be abundant as close to a star as TOI-2535 b is currently.

This means that hot Jupiters likely form far from their stars and then migrate inwards. There are two ways that this could happen. The planet could be excited into an elliptical orbit by violent events like a near-collision with another planetary object, and then interactions with the star pull the planet inwards.

Alternatively, the hot Jupiter may be pulled inwards along with the other planets while sitting in a flattened cloud of gas and dust around the infant star called a protoplanetary disk.

If this second, less turbulent route occurs to bring hot Jupiters close to their stars, then the resultant system should be very flat. In other words, there shouldn't be extreme tilts between the orbits of the planets in that system.

However, the tilt caused to TOI-2535 b by its unseen companion indicates that flattened systems can be twisted by more tilted orbits later in their existence. This makes the slower migration possible despite the orbital tilt.

"Because TOI-2535 b has a close neighbor, it probably migrated by slowly spiraling in instead of getting flung in," Yee said. "We may be seeing a formation channel that doesn’t happen very often but is very interesting."

The team's research was published on Monday (Nov. 9) in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

 <description>Česko zaostává za průměrem zemí OECD v podílu vysokoškolsky vzdělaných lidí. České vysoké školství proto potřebuje reformu, říká zakladatel společnosti PAQ Research v pravidelném pořadu Život k nezaplacení.</description>

</item>

 <description>Vláda posílá do Sněmovny ústavní zákon o celostátním referendu. Aby prošel, potřebovala by koalice ANO, SPD a Motoristů 120 hlasů. V tuto chvíli jich ale tolik nemá.    <description>Předseda STAN Vít Rakušan ve středečních 15 minutách mluvil o tom, že nesouhlasí s případným zavedením sektorových daní.   <item>
   <title>Lepší sazby spořicích účtů? Banky v silné konkurenci soupeří o klienty</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/banky-sazby-sporici-ucty/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Lepší sazby, ale až po splnění řady podmínek. Získat lepší úročení není zadarmo, potvrzují analytici. Základní sazba České národní banky je od minulého týdne na čtyřech procentech, mnohé komerční banky ale na spořicích účtech svým zákazníkům nabízejí ještě o něco lepší úročení. Roli hraje každá desetina procenta.</description>
   <pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:50:15 +0100</pubDate>

  <item>
   <title>Menopauza, urážky, hádky. Rakušan kritizoval poměry ve sněmovně, Ševčík se brání</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/vit-rakusan-kritika-chovani-sevcik-okamura-snemovna/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Vládnoucí koalice se v Poslanecké sněmovně podle předsedy STAN Víta Rakušana buď obává opoziční menšiny, nebo svou většinu uplatňuje brutálním a tvrdým způsobem. V 15 minutách Kateřiny Perknerové na Deník.cz kritizoval poslance Miroslava Ševčíka a předsedu sněmovny Tomia Okamuru. Deník.cz oslovil Ševčíka, který Rakušanova slova odmítl a řekl, že negativní atmosféru ve sněmovně způsobuje naopak opozice. </description>

   <title>Jak mít klidné Vánoce? Nákupní týden s Deníkem vám zajistí dárky včas</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/nakupni-tyden-s-denikem/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Vyhnout se při nákupech vánočních dárků zaplněným obchodům můžete, pokud se na ně vydáte včas. Navíc se slevou tak lze učinit během aktuálního Nákupního týdne Deníku, jehož se účastní řada obchodů s různým sortimentem.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Rakušan k antimonopolnímu úřadu: Doufám, že vláda nedá na to, kdo je čí kamarád</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/vit-rakusan-u-antimonoponiho-uradu-konci-petr-mlsna-vlada-vyberove-rizeni/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Jsem zvědavý, jak vláda naloží s nominačním zákonem, doufám, že dá na odborné kompetence a morální integritu víc než na to, že je někdo něčí kamarád. Předseda STAN Vít Rakušan tak ve středečních 15 minutách Kateřiny Perknerové na Deník.cz reagoval na to, že Petr Mlsna nedostal od Národního bezpečnostního úřadu bezpečnostní prověrku a v prosinci končí ve funkci šéfa antimonopolního úřadu. Vláda na nové obsazení vypsala v úterý výběrové řízení.</description>
   <pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:23:27 +0100</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/vit-rakusan-u-antimonoponiho-uradu-konci-petr-mlsna-vlada-vyberove-rizeni/</guid>

  <item>
   <title>Mirek Topolánek otevřeně: Lucie se mnou ztratila kariéru. Nikdy mi to nevyčítala</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/mirek-topolanek-rodina-manzelka-nemoc/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Mirek Topolánek nikdy nepatřil k mužům, kteří by se omlouvali za každé ostré slovo. Získal si obdivovatele i nesmiřitelné odpůrce a o svá rozhodnutí se dodnes dokáže přít. Jenže když v rozhovoru pro podcast O životě zblízka začne mluvit o své ženě Lucii, zazní věty, které by od něj možná čekal málokdo. O ceně, kterou podle něj zaplatila za jejich společný život, o vlastní zranitelnosti i o tom, proč dnes nechce, aby se k němu chovala jako k pacientovi. Velmi osobní rozhovor s bývalým premiérem přinese Deník.cz ve svém podcastu již v pátek.</description>
   <pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:11:34 +0100</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/mirek-topolanek-rodina-manzelka-nemoc/</guid>
   <category>Česko</category>
   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/54f/54fc958a-23a4-43e9-81dd-bfe2bed85300.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/54f/54fc958a-23a4-43e9-81dd-bfe2bed85300.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Mirek Topolánek přijal pozvání Bohumily Čihákové do podcastu O Životě zblízka. Přinesl s sebou i exkluzivní fotografie z rodinného archivu.</media:description>
    <media:credit>se svolením Matouše Kostkana</media:credit>
   </media:content>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Sázkař z České Lípy měl šťastnou ruku. Tiket zachránila tyč i zákrok v nastavení</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/sazkar-ceska-lipa-vyhra-liga-mistru-stesti-chance/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Pořádnou trefu si připsal jeden ze sázkařů v České Lípě. Na pobočce sázkové kanceláře Chance podal minulý týden tiket na šest fotbalových zápasů Ligy mistrů. Vsadil dva tisíce korun a tipoval vždy vítězství favoritů. Nakonec se mu podařilo uhádnout všech šest výsledků a odnesl si výhru přesahující 55 tisíc korun.</description>
   <pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:03:35 +0100</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Na D8 před Německem se srazil autobus se dvěma náklaďáky, šest zraněných</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/usti/zpravy/hromadna-nehoda-kamiony-zavrena-silnice-chomutovsko.A261111_141454_usti-zpravy_grr#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Na dálnici D8 se odpoledne před hranicí s Německem střetla v husté mlze dvě nákladní auta a patrový autobus. Zranilo se šest cizinců z autobusu. Dálnice byla ve směru na Německo uzavřena. Kolona se rozjela kolem 17:30. Zavřené jsou i nadále ve směru na Německo oba tunely před hranicí. Auta stojí i u hranic s Německem na silnici I/7 na Chomutovsku, kde také bouralo několik aut.</description>
      <pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:09:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/usti/zpravy">Ústí - Ústí - zprávy</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/usti/zpravy/hromadna-nehoda-kamiony-zavrena-silnice-chomutovsko.A261111_141454_usti-zpravy_grr/diskuse</comments>

      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/112/cl6/GRR760daea914_HW2DpVfWMAANTth.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Dopravní nehoda několika vozidel na silnici I/7 na 88. kilometru ve směru na Horu Svatého Šebestiána (11. listopadu 2026)</media:description>
      <media:credit>Policie ČR</media:credit>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Babiš míří do Irska. S lídry EU bude řešit AI a ceny energií, setká se i se Zelenským</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/babis-miri-do-irska-lidri-eu-tam-maji-resit-umelou-inteligenci-i-ceny-energii.A261111_090139_domaci_chtl#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Od našeho zpravodaje v Dublinu – Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) ve středu večer odletěl na dvoudenní cestu do Dublinu. Ve čtvrtek se zúčastní summitu Evropského politického společenství, na němž budou lídři spolu s představiteli klíčových institucí jednat o konkurenceschopnosti Evropy s ohledem na inovace a ceny energií. V pátek ho čeká neformální Evropská rada zaměřená na využití umělé inteligence.</description>
      <pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:39:00 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Nebylo to tak vážné. Soud nepotrestal vychovatelky za hrubé chování k dětem</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/usti/zpravy/soud-rozhodnuti-vychovatelky-deti-jesle-prestupek-radnice-tyrani.A261111_164339_usti-zpravy_grr#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Křik, posměšky ani nevhodné výrazy na adresu batolat nebyly trestným činem. V případu tří zaměstnankyň žateckých jeslí soud v Lounech po více než dvou letech dospěl k závěru, že se sice k dětem chovaly nevhodně, nicméně nešlo o závažné prohřešky. Případ proto soud postoupil radnici v Žatci k projednání přestupku. Rozhodnutí není pravomocné.</description>

      <description>Počet novorozenců v Česku by se podle ředitele Ústavu zdravotnických informací a statistiky (ÚZIS) Ladislava Duška mohl letos snížit pod hranici 75 000 dětí, což by bylo nové minimum.       <description>Polsko si ve středu připomíná obnovu své nezávislosti v roce 1918. Ve Varšavě při této příležitosti vyšly na pochod desetitisíce nacionalistů a stoupenců krajní pravice. Do jejich čela se postavil národněkonzervativní prezident Karol Nawrocki. Oslavy letos provázejí přísnější bezpečnostní opatření. Důvodem je sobotní útok v centru Krakova, při němž mladý Polák šest lidí zastřelil a patnáct zranil.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/z-ceska-zrychluje-rust-umela-inteligence-ktera-hlida-lidska-srdce-jeji-hodnotu-ted-investori-vytahli-na-600-milionu/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Je to pár let, co začali u sklenky vína kardiolog Tomá&#353; Skála a podnikatel Stephen Burke rozebírat způsoby, jak složitě se měří srdeční rytmus. Rozhodli se je změnit, a to tak důkladně, že hodnota jejich nápadu a jeho reálného uskutečnění v podobě medicínsko-technologického startupu Kardi Ai právě dosáhla 600 milionů Kč.</description>

<description>Brno žádá poslance a senátory, aby při změně financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu zachovali zákonné záruky pro regionální studia. Jde o minimální rozsah regionálního vysílání i podíl televizních studií na celoplo&#353;ném programu. Usnesení zastupitelů představila ve středu 11. listopadu na brněnském zasedání Rady České televize první náměstkyně primátora Kamila Zlatu&#353;ková.</description>

 <description>E-mail s bombovou výhrůžkou obdrželo v Itálii na 6000 škol, uvedl ve středu podle médií ministr školství Giuseppe Valditara. Policie zatím v žádné z nich bombu nenalezla. Některé školní budovy nebyly ani evakuované. Bombové výhrůžky dostaly i školy ve Skotsku a v Severním Irsku, kde je policie sice také prověřovala, ale zároveň uvedla, že je nepovažuje za věrohodné.</description>

 <description>Zvláštní američtí vyslanci Steve Witkoff a Jared Kushner ve čtvrtek odcestují do Moskvy, kde se setkají s ruským prezidentem Vladimirem Putinem. Po návštěvě ruské metropole se sejdou s ukrajinským prezidentem Volodymyrem Zelenským v Dublinu. Kushner to podle agentur řekl novinářům v Abú Zabí po skončení dvoudenního jednání zástupců Ruska a Ukrajiny zprostředkovaného USA o možnostech ukončení ruské války proti Ukrajině.</description>

 <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) odmítl spojování dalšího financování pro Ukrajinu s jednáním o víceletém rozpočtu Unie. I slovenský premiér Robert Fico se ohradil proti výzvě německého kancléře Friedricha Merze, aby se všechny země EU zavázaly k podílu na pokrytí schodku ukrajinského rozpočtu v příštím roce. „Německá argumentace je následující. Je v zájmu všech zemí Evropské unie, aby Ukrajina tuhle válku neprohrála,“ říká novinář Ondřej Houska.</description>

<item>
 <title>Rusko rozšiřuje řady svých mezinárodních žoldáků. V Záporoží byl zajat muž z Indonésie</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/rusko-ukrajina-zaporozi-zoldak-indonesie-obchod-s-lidmi_2611111031_elev</link>
 <description>Ukrajinská armáda zajala muže indonéské národnosti, který bojoval na straně Ruska. Jakarta se bojí obchodu s lidmi, ruská strana popírá jakékoliv své zapojení. Ve válce s Ukrajinou se však k této strategii Rusko neuchyluje poprvé. V minulosti šlo hlavně o lidi z Afriky, zemí střední Asie či Indie a Bangladéše.</description>

 <description>Vyjednavače Kyjeva, Moskvy a Washingtonu čekají v Abú Zabí další společná jednání. Minule dojednali výměnu zajatců a návrat ukrajinských dětí do vlasti. „Kamenem úrazu je dohodnutí bezpečnostních záruk a jejich charakteru a také velikost a postavení ukrajinské armády. Tam se zatím pozice zásadně rozcházejí. Rusko nechce na Ukrajině žádné cizí pozorovatelské ani stabilizační síly. Ukrajina naopak požaduje záruky,“ říká generál Pavel Macko.</description>

 <description>Řidič příměstského autobusu v jihokorejském Songnamu narazil během ranní dopravní špičky do více než 30 vozidel stojících na červenou. Bezmála 60 lidí při tom utrpělo zranění, uvedla ve středu agentura AP.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/otec-meghan-markle-je-opet-ve-vazbe-muz-obvineny-z-drzeni-detske-pornografie-si_2611110837_mst</link>
 <description>Otec britské vévodkyně ze Sussexu Thomas Markle je zpět ve vazbě ve federální věznici na Floridě. Markle je obviněný z držení dětské pornografie. Minulý týden byl po svém zatčení umístěn do domácího vězení, v úterý si ale podle soudu sám odřízl elektronický monitorovací náramek z kotníku. Porušil tak podmínky domácí vazby a soud ho poslal do věznice, píše agentura Reuters.</description>

</item>
<item>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/ruska-tajna-sluzba-tvrdi-ze-zadrzela-dva-polske-agenty-vini-je-ze-spionaze-v_2611110729_mst</link>
 <description>Ruská tajná služba FSB oznámila zadržení dvou agentů polských zpravodajských služeb, které viní ze špionáže – konkrétně ze shromažďování informací o vojenských objektech a sociálně-ekonomické situaci v ruské Kaliningradské oblasti, která je vklíněná mezi polským a litevským územím. Uvedla to ve středu ráno agentura Interfax. Mluvčí polského ministra odpovědného za tajné služby označil za provokaci a dezinformaci. </description>

</item>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/demokrate-v-usa-zvitezili-co-ale-republikani-stihnou-do-ledna-zustaneme-pres_2611110700_vdv</link>
 <description>Končícím republikánům v americkém Kongresu zbývá necelých pět jednacích týdnů. Bylo by namístě předpokládat, že strana po historické volební porážce využije zbývající čas k prosazení návrhů, kterými ještě naposledy ovlivní směřování země. Ale zákony, které musejí zákonodárci do konce roku stihnout určitě, se nebezpečně nakupily. Zápas ve Washingtonu se očekává třeba o další financování obrany a války s Íránem.</description>

<description>Je to pár let, co začali u sklenky vína kardiolog Tomá&#353; Skála a podnikatel Stephen Burke rozebírat způsoby, jak složitě se měří srdeční rytmus. Rozhodli se je změnit, a to tak důkladně, že hodnota jejich nápadu a jeho reálného uskutečnění v podobě medicínsko-technologického startupu Kardi Ai právě dosáhla 600 milionů Kč.</description>

<description>Brno žádá poslance a senátory, aby při změně financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu zachovali zákonné záruky pro regionální studia. Jde o minimální rozsah regionálního vysílání i podíl televizních studií na celoplo&#353;ném programu. Usnesení zastupitelů představila ve středu 11. listopadu na brněnském zasedání Rady České televize první náměstkyně primátora Kamila Zlatu&#353;ková.</description>

Autocamp Sedmihorky obhájil titul nejlepšího kempu v Česku.</description></item><item><title>Liberec znovu nabízí zdarma boudičky pro kočky bez domova. Pomáhají jim přežít zimu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905520-liberec-znovu-nabizi-zdarma-boudicky-pro-kocky-bez-domova-pomahaji-jim-prezit-zimu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905520-liberec-znovu-nabizi-zdarma-boudicky-pro-kocky-bez-domova-pomahaji-jim-prezit-zimu.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>S příchodem chladných dnů připravilo město Liberec opět zdarma zateplené polystyrenové boxy pro opuštěné kočky. Vyzvednout si je může každý, kdo chce toulavým zvířatům pomoci překonat zimu. Magistrát zároveň nabízí zajištění kastrace, která účinně zamezuje nekontrolovanému množení opuštěných koček.</description></item><item><title>S čerstvým řidičákem si spletl pedály. V Novém Boru najel do zastávky</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905480-s-cerstvym-ridicakem-si-spletl-pedaly-v-novem-boru-najel-do-zastavky.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905480-s-cerstvym-ridicakem-si-spletl-pedaly-v-novem-boru-najel-do-zastavky.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:34:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Policisté během pondělí na Českolipsku řešili hned dvě podobné nehody, kdy si řidiči spletli brzdový pedál s plynem a havarovali.</description></item><item><title>Změna v čele Libereckého kraje. Martina Půtu má nahradit Jan Sviták</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905479-zmena-v-cele-libereckeho-kraje-putu-ma-nahradit-jan-svitak.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905479-zmena-v-cele-libereckeho-kraje-putu-ma-nahradit-jan-svitak.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:18:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Po čtrnácti letech končí v čele Libereckého kraje hejtman Martin Půta, který míří do Senátu. Klub SLK vybral jako jeho nástupce poslance a bývalého náměstka Jana Svitáka. Ten kvůli nové roli odejde z Poslanecké sněmovny. Volba proběhne 15. prosince.</description></item><item><title>Silnici 13 u Jítravy zablokovala nehoda tří aut. Jeden zraněný</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905474-silnici-13-u-jitravy-zablokovala-nehoda-tri-aut-jeden-zraneny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905474-silnici-13-u-jitravy-zablokovala-nehoda-tri-aut-jeden-zraneny.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Srážka tří aut ráno zablokovala silnici mezi Bílým Kostelem a Jítravou. Silnice byla nějakou dobu zcela uzavřená, poté policisté až do ukončení zásahu řídili dopravu kyvadlově. Při nehodě se zranil jeden člověk.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký cykloboom: Počet výpůjček sdílených kol vzrostl letos na dvojnásobek</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905448-liberecky-cyklobom-pocet-vypujcek-sdilenych-kol-vzrostl-letos-na-dvojnasobek.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905448-liberecky-cyklobom-pocet-vypujcek-sdilenych-kol-vzrostl-letos-na-dvojnasobek.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:59:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Letošní sezóna sdílených kol v Liberci překonala všechna očekávání. Od dubna do října lidé uskutečnili 38 465 jízd, což je více než dvojnásobek oproti loňsku. S nárůstem o 103 % vykazuje Liberec druhý nejrychlejší růst cyklomobility v ČR a vyvrací mýtus, že je město pro kola příliš kopcovité.</description></item><item><title>Stovky litrů vody za sekundu navíc. Přehrada Josefův Důl znásobí své síly</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905356-stovky-litru-vody-za-sekundu-navic-prehrada-josefuv-dul-znasobi-sve-sily.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905356-stovky-litru-vody-za-sekundu-navic-prehrada-josefuv-dul-znasobi-sve-sily.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Vydatné deště a tání sněhu už nepřijdou vniveč. Přehrada Josefův Důl brzy dostane z Jeleního potoka až půl kubíku vody za sekundu navíc. Trubka pod zemí tak zajistí plné kohoutky na Liberecku i Jablonecku, a navíc bude pohánět novou elektrárnu, která vyrobí čistou energii.</description></item><item><title>Chodkyně zemřela v Hejnicích po střetu s osobním autem</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905456-chodkyne-zemrela-v-hejnicich-na-liberecku-po-stretu-s-osobnim-autem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905456-chodkyne-zemrela-v-hejnicich-na-liberecku-po-stretu-s-osobnim-autem.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 20:42:13 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Chodkyně zemřela v úterý v podvečer v Hejnicích po střetu s osobním autem. Tragická nehoda se stala na přechodu pro chodce v Lázeňské ulici, řekli regionální mluvčí policie a záchranné služby.</description></item><item><title>V libereckém Vesci shořelo auto</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905452-v-libereckem-vesci-shorelo-auto.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905452-v-libereckem-vesci-shorelo-auto.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 19:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Hasiči z Liberce vyrazili v úterý dopoledne k požáru osobního auta do čtvrti Vesec. Navíc hrozilo, že se oheň rozšíří na blízké budovy.</description></item><item><title>110 km/h v obci a propadlý řidičák. Hazardér v mercedesu byl rekordmanem kontrol</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905409-110-km-h-v-obci-a-propadly-ridicak-hazarder-v-mercedesu-byl-rekordmanem-kontrol.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905409-110-km-h-v-obci-a-propadly-ridicak-hazarder-v-mercedesu-byl-rekordmanem-kontrol.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 19:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Při dopravní kontrole v Libereckém kraji odhalili policisté 49 řidičů porušujících rychlostní limity. Dva z nich jeli o 60 km/h rychleji – v obci Držkov naměřili řidiči mercedesu 110 km/h a navíc zjistili propadlý řidičák. Akce odhalila i jízdu bez pásů, s mobilem, pod vlivem drog či přes zákaz.</description></item></channel></rss>

      <description>V Číně sice dominují mobilní hry, ale tamní vývojáři se stále víc snaží pronikat na trh AAA titulů. ]]> Vítr z hor – Tobias Piero Dohm: RAUM – ZEIT https://www.vybezek.eu/296639-vitr-z-hor-tobias-piero-dohm-raum-zeit/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:47:57 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296639 V pondělí 9. listopadu 2026 byl zahájen letošní ročník divadelního festivalu Vítr z hor, jako první se představil performer Tobias Piero Dohm v představení RAUM – ZEIT.

Z anotací – Festival Vítr z hor se i letos připojuje k mezinárodní akci La Nuit du Cirque, a přináší do Šluknovského výběžku cirkusový vír fantazie, odvahy a hravosti. A co vás čeká?

Kromě tří dnů Cirkusových nocí 13. – 15. 11. i dvě další novocirkusová představení 9. a 12. listopadu! Nenechte si je ujít! V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 Tobias Piero Dohm (@pieroodo): Raum Zeit. Vizuálně působivá inscenace, v níž se pohybem, objekty a proměnlivým prostorem posouvají hranice mezi tělem, prostředím a časem.

Tma, kouř, koule. Koule skoro všude. A písek…

]]> Festival rostlin v České Kamenici https://www.vybezek.eu/296611-festival-rostlin-v-ceske-kamenici/ Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:26:06 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296611 V sobotu 7. a neděli 8. listopadu 2026 se ve sportovní hale v České Kamenici koná Festival rostlin.

Akce, která pokud vím, tu dosud neměla obdoby. Celá hala plná několika řad regálů a na nich kytky, spousty kytek. Mnohdy takových, jaké jste ještě nejspíš ani neviděli… A davy, odnášející si mnohdy nejednu plnou tašku. Neuvěřitelný výběr. Plus nějaké doplňky.

Pro mne zjištění, že jsem uvázl v minulosti a jsem mimo nejen v náhledu na ceny v restauracích, ale zaspal jsem i cenový vývoj u pokojovek. Vlastně hrůza, jak velké jmění mi za pár let doma různě uschlo…

]]> Parní vlak na trase Drážďany – Moldava a zpět 07. 11. 2026 https://www.vybezek.eu/296569-parni-vlak-na-trase-drazdany-moldava-a-zpet-07-11-2026/ Sat, 07 Nov 2026 13:57:39 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296569 V sobotu 7. listopadu 2026 za hojného zájmu přihlížejících dětí, dospělých i šotoušů zastavila na vlakovém nádraží v Rumburku zase jednou souprava tažená parní lokomotivou (35 1097).

Žst. Rumburk:

Moldavská dráha / Teplický Semmering / „Most – Freiberg“ na FB:

V SOBOTU 7. LISTOPADU VYRAZÍ Z DRÁŽĎAN PARNÍ VLAK NA MOLDAVU!

Železniční muzeum Dresden-Altstadt a spolek Flügelradtouristik pořádají mimořádnou jízdu historického vlaku s oddílovými osobními vozy a jídelním vozem.

Z Drážďan vyrazí v 6:30 s německou parní lokomotivou 35 1097 přes Rumburk a Děčín do Mostu. Zde převezme vlak česká parní lokomotiva 433.001 „Skaličák“, které bude na horské trati pomáhat dieselová lokomotiva.

Most 12:00 – Osek město 12:32 – Dubí 13:22 – Moldava 14:09. Zpět z Moldavy vlak odjede v 15:20 přes Dubí, Louku u Litvínova a Teplice do Drážďan. Část historické soupravy zamíří také do Žatce, města chmele a piva.

Souprava na nádraží doplnila vodu (výpomoc poskytly dva vozy JSDH Brtníky), a posádka provedla na mašině nutný servis (trochu mne zaskočily dva pytle písku, ale má to logické vysvětlení).

Na FB Děčínsko video a info:

Parní vlak v čele s německou lokomotivou 35 1097-1 (vyrobenou v roce 1959 a známou také pod přezdívkou Rübezahl) projel v sobotu dopoledne těsně před desátou hodinou po železničním mostě mezi Děčínem východ a hlavním nádražím. Pohled na tuto historickou soupravu z nové lávky pro pěší a cyklisty.
